title: explain_null_value is dead code — fully implemented and tested but never called by any production path
description: explain_null_value is a public-looking enricher that produces human-readable null-origin explanations, but nothing in src/ ever calls it. It is not invoked by enrich_steps or any node-type enricher, not re-exported via haute.trace or haute.__init__, and not reached by any dynamic/string dispatch. Its only references are its own definition and a dedicated test class (tests/test_trace_enrichment.py:2601+). It therefore inflates the module and its line/branch coverage without contributing to any traced behaviour. Per the project's dead-code guidance (raise coverage by deleting dead code, not by gaming the gate), this is a removal candidate (function + its tests).
evidence: Repo-wide search for non-definition, non-test references returns nothing: `grep -rn explain_null_value --include=*.py . | grep -v tests/ | grep -v 'def explain_null_value'` => only the def at line 62. No hit in src/haute/trace.py or src/haute/__init__.py. No getattr/string-keyed dispatch references it (the only `null_value`/`fill_null` hits are unrelated, in chunking.py:439/455). The five other private banding/payload helpers in this file (_banding_factor_for_column, _banding_*_payload, _focus_banding_factor, _copy_banding_factor_summary) all have real callers at lines 462/584/586/1101-1104/1207-1212; explain_null_value uniquely has none.
est_reduction: ~38 lines in src (the function + its module section header) plus the associated test class; net coverage neutral-to-positive since the removed code currently only pads coverage via its own tests.
behavior_preservation: Removing the function and its tests changes no runtime behaviour because no production code imports or calls it. (If it is intended as public API, it should instead be wired into the null-explanation path or exported and documented — currently it is neither.)
